hypothesis: A fresh completed-five-minute RSI(14) crossover of its EMA(7) against an open HYPE breakout position may exit deteriorating momentum earlier than the active eight-hour soft boundary while preserving the venue stop as the authoritative safety exit.
decision: Reject this exact completed-5m RSI14/EMA7 momentum-reversal exit for promotion. Under the identical reconstructed HYPE entry stream, next-open execution, fees, slippage, funding, and venue-stop precedence, it reduced net return and increased maximum drawdown in both development and the already-opened final 60-day block. Preserve the active v14 exit contract, grant this challenger no execution authority, and do not tune variants against the opened final block.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen completed-5m momentum exit evaluated on fresh profile-matched live lifecycles would update this rejection if it improves after-cost return and drawdown across multiple non-adjacent windows without materially increasing fees or converting recoverable holds into losses. Changed source-file hashes, noncausal higher-timeframe values, same-bar fills, or a venue stop losing precedence would invalidate the present comparison.
limitations: The final 60-day block was already opened by prior work and is descriptive rather than a sealed confirmation sample.

The common historical entry stream is intentionally identical between arms but is much broader than the sparse currently resolved live HYPE sample, so its absolute profitability does not establish or disprove the live entry edge.
One-minute bars cannot reproduce intraminute stop ordering, private queue position, IOC latency, or every realized fill.
Different exit timing changes position occupancy and therefore the number of later entry signals each arm can accept.
The experiment rejects one exact momentum rule; it does not prove that every state-aware exit is harmful.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, sizing policy, backend process, checkpoint process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
